cues.text: Suits are often the most expensive thing a customer brings in. Here is how to check one and pack it the right way.
First, the jacket and pants have the same tag number, and it matches the ticket.
Check that both pieces are the same fabric and color. Navy and black are easy to mix up, so look closely in good light.
The pants have one sharp crease on each leg, with no double lines, and even cuffs.
The lapels should roll softly, not be pressed flat. No shiny marks on the shoulders or lapels.
Use a wide suit hanger with a bar, never a thin wire hanger. Thin hangers leave bumps in the shoulders.
Fold the pants over the bar along their creases, so the creases stay sharp.
Put the jacket on the hanger so the shoulders sit right on the ends of the hanger.
Button the top button of the jacket, and make sure pocket flaps are out, not tucked in.
If there is a vest, it goes on the same hanger, under the jacket.
Bag it all together, with the ticket on the outside. One suit, one hanger, one bag.
This is what a finished suit looks like: shoulders sitting on the hanger, top button closed, pants folded on the crease underneath.
